title: CoHog+ Adversarial Reciprocity and Competitive-Gap Inversion
thesis: Reward independently useful challenges, including competitor challenges, so the challenger and the challenged both gain while the public commons improves.

distinctions.capability_gap: Difference in demonstrated capability, learning speed, resilience, or usefulness.
distinctions.participation_gap: Barrier to discovering, testing, contributing, reusing, or receiving benefits.
distinctions.goal: Improve aggregate capability while lowering legitimate participation barriers, not necessarily to dominate competitors.

cycle: Publish bounded falsifiable claims and interfaces
Invite independent attacks and alternative hypotheses
Receive evidence with consent and safe disclosure controls
Reward contribution according to verified marginal value
Publish a redacted, source-bound fix and a challenge receipt
Re-test against fresh adversaries and monitor regressions
co_seed: Each challenge is a versioned hypothesis with provenance, safety classification, custody and expected impact.
co_path: Challenge -> Triage -> Reproduce -> Repair -> Verify -> Credit -> Share -> Rechallenge
inversions: Attack becomes quality assurance rather than mere damage.
Competitor becomes a possible paid contributor without surrendering independence.
A failure receipt becomes a reusable public seed.
Disagreement becomes evidence-producing collaboration rather than enforced consensus.
Open participation can strengthen the system even when proprietary advantage declines.
An apparently harmful critique may expose a higher-value alternative, but only after independent verification.
reward_principles: Pay for independently verified improvement, not number or severity of unverified allegations.
Protect responsible disclosure and privacy; do not pay for destructive exploitation, harassment, or coercion.
Offer recognition, reciprocal access, grants or monetary bounties only when funded and explicitly authorized.
Publish adjudication criteria and appeals; prevent capture by repeat insiders.
Do not make acceptance conditional on agreement with CoCivium ideology.
falsifiers: Challenge costs exceed reproducible improvements for sustained periods.
Rewards induce fabricated vulnerabilities or gaming.
Adversarial participation decreases after sharing improvements.
The participation gap widens or access becomes more coercive.
Open sharing destroys operational viability without offsetting public gains.
Claims of superior learning lack independent benchmarks.
gdside: Permitted as a clearly labeled philosophical or value-hypothesis lens; not empirical proof or a substitute for consent, safety, or independent verification.
governance: No autonomous payouts, security testing of third parties, public allegations, or publication of sensitive exploit details. Such actions require scoped permission and human authorization.
acceptance: A permitted benign challenge is independently reproduced and receives a source-bound receipt.
A rejected challenge preserves its reasoning and appeal path.
A public improvement is discoverable by an unaffiliated consumer.
Attribution and benefit sharing can be audited.
A malicious or privacy-invasive submission is held safely without public leakage.
proof_boundary: This file is a design artifact, not an implemented reward program, active bounty, measured competitive advantage, or verified public benefit.
